key_insight: Scal3R applies scalable test-time training to large-scale 3D reconstruction, allowing feed-forward models to adapt on-the-fly to long video sequences so they preserve geometric accuracy and cross-sequence consistency by capturing global contextual cues.
problem_solved: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models lose accuracy and consistency on long video sequences because of limited memory and insufficient mechanisms to aggregate global context; Scal3R addresses how to scale adaptation and context aggregation at test time.
method: Run lightweight test-time training during inference so the model incrementally adapts to incoming frames rather than relying on a single static forward pass.
Maintain a memory-efficient global context representation (compressed / hierarchical aggregation) that summarizes long-range scene information without unbounded memory growth.
Use incremental / sliding-window updates and consistency regularization to stabilize reconstructions across long sequences while keeping compute and memory manageable.
impact: Enables robust, consistent large-scale 3D reconstructions from long videos — important for mapping, robotics, AR/VR and any application requiring reliable scene geometry over extended captures. Practitioners get a practical route to scale test-time adaptation without prohibitive memory or compute.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming video -> test-time training loop -> updated model + global context -> reconstructed 3D scene

paper_title: Scal3R: Scalable Test-Time Training for Large-Scale 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Tao Xie, Peishan Yang, Yudong Jin, Yingfeng Cai, Wei Yin
